Question: How do I disciple someone else?
ShortAnswer: Discipling someone means walking with them as they learn to follow Jesus: studying Scripture together, praying together, modeling obedience, and helping them grow until they can do the same for someone else.
DetailedAnswer: Jesus' model of discipleship was life-on-life: He called twelve people to be with Him, taught them, sent them out, and corrected them along the way (Mark 3:14). Paul passed the same pattern on: 'what you have heard from me... entrust to reliable people who will also be qualified to teach others' (2 Timothy 2:2). Practically, discipling someone often looks ordinary: meet regularly, read a book of the Bible together and talk honestly about what it means, pray for each other's struggles, and share your own life — including your failures. You do not need to be an expert; you need to be a few steps ahead and willing to be honest. Ask good questions, listen well, point them to Christ rather than to yourself, and celebrate growth. And keep the goal in view: a disciple is not someone who depends on you forever, but someone who learns to depend on Jesus — and in time, to disciple someone else.
